Pass with caveats. DASS-21 administered in Dutch to a Dutch community sample; neither the deposit (dataverse.nl doi:10.34894/CMJXAK; only Data_total.csv and a variable-information codebook whose sole DASS entry reads 'DASS;Depression Anxiety Stress Scale - 21 (DASS-21)') nor the PLOS ONE paper's S1-S4 appendices (SVC only) carry any DASS item wording, so there are no data labels and no study-supplied text. Item wording shipped from the instrument's own site (www2.psy.unsw.edu.au/dass): administered-language field = the de Beurs Dutch DASS21, REVISED 2010 (Dutch/DASS21 Dutch revised.pdf, sha256 8a298b98aecf029bac6d171b896947b581370259c9d2a05123151abc4dd89bd8); _translated field = the official English DASS21 (Download files/Dass21.pdf, sha256 8644cc86534d397e371985d5b25422ba76c4cdae0a5aed8f1a4453c17a5cd393). VERSION INFERENCE: the study names no Dutch translation (it cites only Lovibond & Lovibond 1995), and the DASS site distributes two Dutch DASS21 forms, stating 'Note that the first 3 items of the Dutch DASS21 differ from the English version, although they belong to the same scales.' The 2010 revision was chosen on three data signals, all in verify_neurodegenerative_huizinga_2019_dass.R: DASS.1 corrected r is stress .618 vs anxiety .448 (the 2001 form's item 1 is DASS-42 #29, which de Beurs 2001 Table 1 loads .50 anxiety / .51 stress, i.e. co-equal); DASS.2 is the weakest item in the pool (max item-scale r .329, D .321 / A .329 / S .322, no anxiety-specific pattern), matching dry mouth (#02, A .43 / S .09) rather than sweating (#19, A .57 / S .11); and DASS.2 is the most endorsed anxiety item (mean .502 vs .154-.295), as dry mouth characteristically is. Item 3's two candidate Dutch wordings ('enig plezier' vs 'enig positief gevoel') are both depression items with near-identical loadings and are NOT separated by any check. OPTION TEXT: both Dutch forms carry identical anchors, so the four option strings are certain; the paper's own English gloss of them is terser ('never' (0), 'sometimes' (1), 'often' (2), 'very often' (3)) than the official English shipped in option_text_translated, which is the instrument publisher's parallel wording rather than a translation of the Dutch. INSTRUCTIONS: shipped verbatim from the Dutch form and therefore say 'door een nummer te omcirkelen' (by circling a number), while this study administered the battery online. RIGHTS: no restriction; the DASS home page (http://www2.psy.unsw.edu.au/dass/, sha256 8daaa45627b4ff7e4d60c90087c8cc9af79efdea675e28fbc3f5e9b996e82aa2, fetched 2026-09-09) states 'The DASS questionnaire is in the public domain, and may be downloaded from this website.' The $55 fee named on that page is for the DASS manual, not the questionnaire. Step 3b: live data is 21 items x resp 0-3, matching DASS-21 and not any sibling instrument in the battery.
